rationale: statfs03 is a 38-line test with a single assertion -- statfs(2) on a path whose prefix denies search permission must fail EACCES -- and its failure traces to one missing conditional in one function. Reading kernel/src/fs/vfs/fs_apis/inode.rs:573-625, the CAP_DAC_OVERRIDE branch of Inode::check_permission strips MAY_READ|MAY_WRITE and then applies Linux's 'executable DACs are overridable only when at least one exec bit is set' rule to every inode type. Linux exempts directories from that rule: generic_permission() returns 0 for a directory whenever CAP_DAC_OVERRIDE holds, and only applies the exec-bit condition on the non-directory fallthrough. So the test's setup, running as root, cannot create TEMP_DIR2 ('testdir/subdir', 0444) inside the mode-0444 'testdir': check_dir_entry_mutation (kernel/src/fs/vfs/path/mod.rs:265-269) asks for MAY_WRITE|MAY_EXEC, DAC override reduces that to MAY_EXEC, testdir has no exec bits, and the call is refused with EACCES -- the same rule also blocks the lookup of 'subdir' at resolver.rs:558. The test dies in setup before reaching its assertion. Search permission itself is already enforced (resolver.rs:558), and fsuid correctly tracks euid (credentials_.rs:299), so once setup can run the unprivileged statfs should already produce the EACCES the test wants. That makes this narrow syscall/permission semantics against a documented Linux rule rather than a subsystem Asterinas lacks, and the DAC-override directory rule is the single localized defect. Chosen over the alternatives I examined for exactly that narrowness: creat08/open10/creat09 and mkdir09 all reduce to S_ISGID inheritance, which run-YIMPAV's committed 'Implement S_ISGID inheritance for new inodes in VFS layer' already fixes tree-wide; fdatasync02's EINVAL-on-special-file is already covered by run-7UHmXC's fsync03 fix, whose diagnosis explicitly names sys_fdatasync/sync_data; epoll_ctl04 and epoll_ctl05 need real epoll nesting-depth and loop detection (Linux's ep_loop_check), a graph traversal Asterinas has no equivalent of; abort01 and waitpid01 both hinge on WCOREDUMP, and no core-dump bit exists anywhere in the process tree, so RLIMIT_CORE being 0/RLIM_INFINITY at rlimit.rs:55 means they demand a core-dump feature; fcntl27 needs F_SETLEASE, fcntl17/23 need lock deadlock detection, prctl10 needs x86 TSC gating, and mincore/mlock/munlock/remap_file_pages/splice/tee all look like absent features; getcpu01 depends on sched_setaffinity actually migrating a thread, which sched_affinity.rs:37-61 only stores a mask for, making it a scheduler change; the socket-side failures (accept/connect/recv/send/sendto/setsockopt/shutdown) sit near the INADDR_ANY gap that got run-OgXQbF's getsockopt01 abandoned as missing-feature. setpriority01 was left alone as adjacent to committed setpriority02, and fdatasync02/creat08/open10 as adjacent to committed work.
